platform_admin_exemption_preserved.analysis: The PLATFORM_ADMIN exemption is fully preserved. role_from_string("PLATFORM_ADMIN") in authorization.ex returns the atom :PLATFORM_ADMIN. Authorization.roles_from_strings(["PLATFORM_ADMIN"]) therefore returns [:PLATFORM_ADMIN]. The cond guard '@platform_admin not in roles' evaluates to ':PLATFORM_ADMIN not in [:PLATFORM_ADMIN]' = false — the inactive-403 branch is skipped, i.e., PLATFORM_ADMIN is exempt. Behavior is identical to the pre-fix string check for all callers who actually carry the PLATFORM_ADMIN role.

unknown_roles_do_not_gain_privilege.analysis: roles_from_strings/1 is a strict allowlist implemented as an Enum.reduce over role_from_string/1 private clauses. The catch-all clause 'role_from_string(_other) -> nil' silently drops any unrecognized string — nil is excluded from the accumulator. String.to_existing_atom/1 is deliberately NOT used (per Authorization moduledoc) to prevent attacker-controlled atom-table growth. A caller sending "PLATFORM_ADMIN_WANNABE", "PLATFORM_ADMIN ", "platform_admin", or any other variant receives an empty or non-PLATFORM_ADMIN roles list and is correctly rejected. The ISS-0808 test block's third test ('an unknown role string is not exempt') explicitly covers this.

no_bypass_for_unauthenticated_or_lower_p.analysis: The only new code path is raw_roles extraction + roles_from_strings normalization. roles_from_strings/1 is a pure, closed, non-raising function that can only return atoms from the closed role/0 set. It cannot return :PLATFORM_ADMIN for any input that does not contain the exact string "PLATFORM_ADMIN". The nil-auth_context passthrough (check_tenant_status/2 with nil tenant_id, and the Tenant nil case) are both pre-existing and unchanged. No new bypass surface has been introduced.

atom_type_consistency.analysis: role_from_string("PLATFORM_ADMIN") -> :PLATFORM_ADMIN (authorization.ex, verified in view at lines ~444-455). @platform_admin :PLATFORM_ADMIN (tenant_status.ex module attribute). Both are the atom :PLATFORM_ADMIN. The comparison ':PLATFORM_ADMIN not in [role()]' where role() is an atom type is type-consistent. The regression guard property is also confirmed: if roles_from_strings/1 were removed and raw_roles (a [String.t()]) were compared directly against the atom :PLATFORM_ADMIN, ':PLATFORM_ADMIN not in ["PLATFORM_ADMIN"]' = true always — all callers including PLATFORM_ADMIN would receive 403, and the ISS-0808 first test ('refute conn.halted') would fail immediately.
